ordered_choices.reason: Extend the aminoenoate's measured 1/1 response to 10/1 without changing sample preparation or flow. This anchors the predicted rise in both endpoints across a large group of rows.
The unmeasured ethyl acetoacetate curve predicts little change from 10/1 to 20/1. A weak-eluent anchor will inform its many loading and flow variants and test transfer from other acetoacetates.
Measure whether the acetylenic diester retains an early front in weak eluent. Its predicted V1 and V2 respond differently, and the measured saturated diesters are imperfect guides.
Dibenzoylmethane has many candidate rows but only a pure-EA measurement. Holding its reagent and loading fixed makes this a direct test of the predicted modest delay at 20/1.
At 1/1 the model puts the end of elution later than the measured end at 5/1, despite predicting an earlier start. Resolve the two endpoint responses for this multifunctional ester.

Anchor the unmeasured chlorobenzophenone at the ratio where substituted benzophenones can elute very late. The result can constrain how strongly the model transfers the methoxy analogue's response to a chloro substituent.
For acetonaphthone, 20/1 lies between a much earlier 10/1 prediction and a later 50/1 prediction. Locate that rise for a fused-ring ketone rather than assuming transfer from monocyclic acetophenones.
A midrange label for the unmeasured fused lactone informs both sides of its solvent curve. It also supplies a cyclic ester example distinct from the better represented benzoates and cyclic ketones.
Bromobenzofuran still starts near 5 mL at 20/1. Determine how much later the extra ring oxygen places the methylenedioxy analogue, informing its unsampled weak-eluent rows.

Anchor the ether-bearing phenoxyethyl acrylate between simple aromatic acrylates and more polar alkoxyethyl esters. At 10/1 the predicted end shifts more than the start, a distinction useful across this series.

Supply a weak-eluent endpoint pair for an unmeasured secondary benzylic alcohol. This distinguishes its retention from that of primary and sterically shielded alcohols and constrains its intermediate ratios.
For this primary alcohol the model predicts later start and end volumes at 1/1 than at 2/1. Test that strong-eluent region before transferring the same response shape across phenylalkanols.
Methyl mandelate combines an exposed hydroxyl and an ester under a relatively large DCM loading volume. Measure its 10/1 interval rather than inferring it from simple alcohols or esters alone.
Quinoline and methylquinoline both lack labels. A 5/1 quinoline measurement will anchor that pair where the available lutidine measurement shows substantial tailing.
The model predicts early, fairly narrow elution for the free bromopropionic acid. A moderate-ratio label tests whether transfer from bromoesters misses an acid-specific shift in V2.

Use one label for branched ethyl bromoisobutyrate to connect the unmeasured branched ester series to measured bromoacetate and bromopropionate. Additional flow variants would not provide a separate model-input contrast.

Reduce sample volume from 150 to 50 µL at fixed DCM volume. Determine whether the measured early front and late end at 20/1 persist at lower loading; the existing 2/1 load pair alone cannot answer this.
Reduce the DCM loading-solvent volume from 500 to 300 µL while retaining the 50 µL sample. This tests whether the broad measured 1/1 interval should transfer between the two preparation series.
The model predicts a pronounced delay at 1/1 for dibenzylideneacetone and a smaller delay for chalcone. One label tests whether to transfer this unusual response across conjugated aryl carbonyls.
At 50/1 the dimethylbenzonitrile prediction puts V1 earlier but V2 later than measured for o-tolunitrile. Test interval broadening rather than transferring a single retention shift to both endpoints.
Anchor the late predicted end volume of para-aminobenzonitrile. The related meta isomer has a broad measured interval at 2/1, but neither isomer has a measured 5/1 response.
Measure the solvent-response span from 2/1 to 20/1 for para-nitrobenzaldehyde at fixed loading. The ortho isomer provides a measured weak-eluent comparison for learning positional effects.

Anchor bromonitrobenzene without a second carbonyl functionality. Its weak-eluent response helps distinguish nitro substitution from the combined effects represented by nitroaldehydes and nitroketones.

The biphenyl aldehyde is predicted to elute much later but over a narrower interval at 20/1 than at 10/1. Measure whether that shape transfers beyond the nearly coincident recorded endpoints of naphthaldehyde.
Provide a strong-eluent anchor for para-aminobenzoate between its predicted 1/1 and 5/1 responses. The measured meta and ortho analogues alone do not establish how position affects the two endpoints.
Anisaldehyde has only a strong-eluent label, while its predicted start rises steeply between 20/1 and 50/1. A second anchor constrains that extrapolation for methoxy-substituted aldehydes.

Give the model a pure-EA reference for a bulky nonpolar polyaryl compound. It complements the retained polar compounds in the batch and can inform the analogous unlabeled bromotriphenylethylene condition.
Compare a flexible branched acrylate with the measured bicyclic acrylate at 50/1. This anchors weak-eluent retention for the unmeasured chain geometry rather than relying on similar lipophilicity.
Anchor the closely spaced PE-rich benzoate series at 40/1, beyond the measured ratios of isobutyl benzoate. This informs nearby solvent ratios without spending labels on flow-only duplicates.
The oxime has measured early elution in strong solvents but a steep predicted increase in both volumes in weak solvent. A fixed-load 20/1 measurement anchors the unsampled portion of its response.

Extend the fixed-load salicylaldehyde series beyond 5/1 and 10/1. Its measured interval is already broad there; the 50/1 result can inform weak-solvent predictions for several ortho-hydroxy aldehydes.

Diethyl malonate has an early, narrow measured interval at 50/1 but a much later end at 1/1 under different conditions. Measure 20/1 at the 1/1 loading and flow to constrain interpolation across its many rows.

batch_review: The batch contains 32 distinct eligible rows on 32 structures. Weak-eluent anchors are balanced by strong- and intermediate-eluent measurements where the predicted interval shape is in question. The sample-volume and DCM-volume contrasts each hold the other axis fixed; no selection repeats a model input solely to vary flow.
batch_strategy: Anchor unmeasured structures where one label can inform several neighboring rows, and extend measured solvent-response curves where related compounds give competing predictions. Reserve two runs for controlled tests of sample volume and loading-solvent volume, which the model represents but often predicts to have little effect.

ordered_choices.reason: At the same loading, measured V2 rose from 19.1 to 43.9 mL between 1/1 and 5/1. The 10/1 center is 44.8 mL. This tests where the solvent response levels off for a multifunctional ester.

The phenoxyethyl acrylate has a measured V2 of 11.4 mL at 10/1 and a center of 41.1 mL at 50/1. A second label constrains the weak-eluent response for ether-containing acrylates. Recorded flow also differs.

A first measurement on this aliphatic chloroketone would constrain its 10/1 through 50/1 predictions. The measured chloroalkyl aryl ketone provides a comparison for how the model transfers carbonyl retention across scaffolds.

The unmeasured acetoxybenzaldehyde has a V2 center of 61.3 mL here. Together with the planned methoxybenzaldehyde measurement at the same ratio, this gives the model labels for two distinct oxygen substituents on an aldehyde scaffold.

The measured 2,4-dimethylacetophenone started at 8.5 mL and ended at 38.6 mL at 50/1. Measuring the 2,4,6-trimethyl analogue tests whether a second ortho methyl group changes onset and interval width, informing the unmeasured alkylated ketone series.

This first aminoacetophenone label extends the measured 2/1 comparison among aminoaromatics to a ketone. The nearby amino ester and aminonitrile have similar measured onsets but different end volumes.

The existing pure-EA measurement fixes the early endpoint for nitroacetophenone. A matched 20/1 measurement constrains its ratio response and tests transfer from the late-eluting para-nitrobenzaldehyde at that ratio.

For unmeasured acetylfluorene the centers are 10.6 and 44.7 mL. Acetonaphthone at 20/1 measured 20.3 and 37.5 mL. This tests transfer of onset and interval width between fused-ring ketones under their recorded preparations.

A first label for 1-phenylethanol anchors the secondary benzylic alcohol series at 10/1. Its close homologue showed substantial retention at 20/1, and the target pool contains several alcohols with only EA-rich measurements.

This fills the gap between matched 1/1 and 10/1 measurements with V2 values of 21.2 and 60.5 mL. The intermediate label can inform many enamine rows spanning two loading solvents and several sample volumes.
At fixed loading, ethyl 4-methoxybenzoate ended at 13.2 and 19.7 mL at 2/1 and 10/1. The 50/1 center reaches 77.2 mL. This measurement constrains the extrapolation for substituted benzoates.

The cyclopropyl ketoester has no measurements. Its 20/1 V2 center of 59.0 mL is close to the 64.4 mL measured for ethyl acetoacetate. A label here tests transfer to a cyclic substituent across the ketoester pool.

Methyl acetoacetate ended at 34.1 mL at 10/1. A matched 50/1 measurement establishes how far that response continues for the small linear ester and complements the cyclic ketoester measurement at 20/1.
Methyl mandelate measured 39.0 and 58.0 mL at 10/1. Its current 2/1 centers are 6.5 and 15.2 mL. This matched point constrains the extent of the decrease for an ester with a benzylic hydroxyl.

This adds a first label for a benzoate bearing a bulky alkyl group on the ring. It extends coverage from benzoates with branched ester chains and anchors predictions for the PE-loaded rows of this structure.
Anisic aldehyde has measured V2 values of 12.6 mL at 2/1 and 117.5 mL at 50/1. The 10/1 label locates the rise between them while matching the sample preparation of the 50/1 measurement.

For 1,4-dimethoxybenzene, weakening the eluent from the measured 20/1 to 50/1 moves the V2 center from a measured 15.7 mL to a predicted 59.1 mL. This matched test informs weak-eluent predictions for dialkoxyarenes.
This is the 500 µL DCM arm of the 5/1 pair at 50 µL sample volume. It carries the higher-volume preparation from the measured 1/1 comparison to a weaker eluent.
The 300 µL DCM arm completes the ratio-by-preparation comparison. The two 5/1 V2 centers differ by only 0.006 mL, whereas the measured 1/1 endpoints differed by 17.8 mL.
At 150 µL, lutidine ended at 26.2 mL at 1/1 and 46.4 mL at 5/1. Its 20/1 center falls to 30.0 mL. Testing this reversal informs solvent-response predictions for basic heteroaromatics.

A first methylquinoline measurement gives the model a second fused nitrogen heterocycle at a ratio where the quinoline response is unresolved. The planned quinoline row provides a same-ratio comparison under its own loading solvent.
Diiodobenzene has no labels and a 900 µL DCM loading preparation. A central-ratio measurement anchors its many rows and extends coverage of early-eluting iodinated aromatics to this preparation.

The meta-aminonitrile ended at 31.6 mL at 2/1. Its 5/1 label gives both a matched ratio contrast and a comparison with the para isomer, which ended at 98.4 mL at 5/1 under the same loading preparation.
The 150 µL arm extends the nitrobenzophenone preparation that ended at 57.0 mL at 20/1. Its paired 50 µL row makes the sample-loading response measurable at 50/1.

The 50 µL arm extends the preparation that ended at 8.5 mL at 20/1. Both 50/1 centers are near 57 mL, so this pair can distinguish persistent load dependence from a difference confined to the earlier measurements.
This first label for the dihydrobenzofuran aldehyde samples a ring ether at a ratio shared by many oxygenated aromatics. It tests transfer from methoxybenzaldehydes to a constrained ether geometry.

Diphenyl sulfoxide introduces an unmeasured polar group on a familiar diaryl scaffold. At 5/1 the label can distinguish its silica retention from that of diaryl carbonyl compounds and constrain its stronger-eluent rows.

The first nitrophenethyl alcohol label tests transfer from both nitroaromatic and primary alcohol measurements in the EA-rich portion of the pool. The para-nitrobenzaldehyde comparison also uses 150 µL sample at 2/1.

A first label for the phosphorus-containing structure tests its predicted 7.7–17.1 mL interval. This supplies a retention measurement for a bonding environment poorly represented among the observed structures and shared by all its ratio variants.
At fixed sample volume, both 1/1 centers are later than the measured 2/1 endpoints for naphthalenemethanol. This tests the local reversal where a related naphthalene alcohol also eluted late at 1/1.

Naphthalene started near 5 mL at 0/1, 2/1 and 10/1. At 50/1 its centers are V1 12.897 and V2 12.553 mL. This matched point tests the predicted onset shift across several weak-eluent rows for a common nonpolar scaffold.

Quinoline ended at 57.7 mL at 5/1. Its 10/1 centers predict a later onset but an earlier end. Holding the loading preparation fixed tests that interval contraction and gives context for the methylquinoline label.

batch_review: The 32 unique eligible IDs cover 30 structures. Each repeated structure completes a two-ratio comparison with one recorded preparation axis varied within each ratio. The other selections cover first measurements, intermediate solvent strengths, weak-eluent extrapolations and an early-eluting hydrocarbon. Strict contrasts match every other recorded condition, and cross-molecule comparisons retain their preparation differences.
batch_strategy: Use matched ratio changes to learn how V1 and V2 respond across common functional groups, and give unmeasured structures their first label where related compounds show different responses. Two paired designs test preparation and loading effects that the model can represent and that could affect predictions across several rows.

hypothesis_updates.claim: At 50 µL sample volume, M-0126 has a later V2 with 500 µL of loading DCM than with 300 µL at both 1/1 and 5/1.
hypothesis_updates.relevance_to_model_learning: The matched comparison supplies labels for the interaction between two model inputs, mobile-phase ratio and loading-solvent volume.
hypothesis_updates.revision_reason: The new 300 µL DCM measurement at 1/1 ended at 18.35 mL, compared with 36.14 mL for 500 µL of DCM. The current 5/1 centers are nearly equal.
hypothesis_updates.unresolved_question: Does the observed ordering of V2 recur at 5/1 with sample volume held fixed?

hypothesis_updates.claim: For M-0178 at both 20/1 and 50/1, V2 at 150 µL sample volume exceeds V2 at 50 µL by at least 20 mL.
hypothesis_updates.relevance_to_model_learning: The paired labels test whether nominal loading helps predict V2 at weak eluent strength. Current 50/1 centers differ by only 0.063 mL between the two loads.
hypothesis_updates.revision_reason: The new 50 µL result gives a measured difference of 48.5 mL at 20/1. At 2/1 the corresponding difference was about −2.0 mL, limiting the claim to weak eluents.
hypothesis_updates.unresolved_question: Does the large positive difference recur at 50/1 when density and loading-solvent preparation are held fixed?

feedback_interpretation: The acquisition-time predictor underestimated V2 by 72.5 mL for anisic aldehyde at 50/1 and 48.5 mL for para-aminobenzonitrile at 5/1. These outcomes motivate an intermediate ratio for the aldehyde and an isomer comparison for the aminonitrile. Nitrobenzophenone supplied a counterexample: its 50 µL run at 20/1 ended at 8.5 mL, 43.7 mL earlier than predicted at acquisition, while the measured 150 µL run ended at 57.0 mL. Dimethoxybenzaldehyde likewise showed a preparation-dependent difference worth testing at a second ratio.

batch_review: The batch contains 32 unique current candidate IDs. Five within-molecule pairs isolate one recorded axis, one pair tests aminobenzonitrile isomer transfer, and the remaining labels cover ratio response, observed failure regimes, and six molecule-novel structures. Repeated loading contrasts span distinct chemotypes and serve separate transfer questions.
batch_strategy: Use matched within-molecule labels to learn sample-loading and loading-solvent-volume interactions, ratio response around observed failure transitions, and transfer across aminobenzonitrile and quinoline analogues. Balance these targeted contrasts with six molecule-novel labels at chemically anchored conditions so graph representations gain broader coverage.

hypothesis_updates.claim: At matched 5/1 chromatography conditions, para-aminobenzonitrile has later V1 and V2 than meta-aminobenzonitrile.
hypothesis_updates.relevance_to_model_learning: The paired labels test positional-isomer structure-condition transfer across sample loading.
hypothesis_updates.revision_reason: The measured matched isomer rows differ in both targets, and the selected 150 µL pair tests whether the ordering transfers with sample loading.
hypothesis_updates.unresolved_question: Does the para-over-meta ordering persist at 150 µL under the same 5/1 DCM 400 µL condition?

feedback_interpretation: Round-1 feedback showed preparation-dependent behavior for M-0126, a strong but ratio-dependent loading effect for M-0178, and a large para-versus-meta aminobenzonitrile difference. It also identified broad failures in nitro carbonyls and nitrogen heteroaromatics. This plan continues those questions with matched contrasts and adds intermediate-ratio and molecule-novel labels for transfer.
